recipes.name: White Chicken Chili with Salsa
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound pepperjack cheese, cut into chunks
1 (8 ounce) can white meat chicken, shredded

steps.text: Combine great Northern beans, salsa, pepper Jack cheese, and chicken in a slow cooker; mix well. Cover the slow cooker.
Cook on Low until cheese has completely melted into chili and flavors have combined, 4 to 5 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: White Chicken Chili with Salsa
raw_recipe.description: This white chicken chili with salsa recipe features tender chicken simmered in the slow cooker with great Northern beans, salsa, and pepper Jack cheese.

review.reviewBody: When I first saw this recipe I didn't have much expectations for it. If anything I thought it would be severely lacking in flavour. I was pleasantly surprised that something SO simple could be SO good! I only made a subtle change and that was to use boneless, skinless chicken breasts that I pre-boiled. I will absolutely make this again!!! THANKS FOR THE SHARE!

It's kind of hard to believe how easy this is. I was happy to find a recipe that would allow me to use up the bag of dried great northern beans my grandma sent home with me on my last visit. This recipe uses about 1/2 a bag of dried northern beans. I bought a 24 oz. jar of salsa. I just went ahead and used the entire thing since there was so little left over. I bought 12.5 oz. can of chicken breast and used it all, including the water it was packed in. It was a long process, making the beans from a bag - rinsing them off, soaking them for 8 hours, quick rinse again, and then boiling them for one hour. The entire process beginning to end using dry beans is 13 1/2-14 hours. Whether you use the jar or dried beans though, it's all mostly hands-off prep, which is great for busy people. I like to smash some of the beans before putting them in the crock pot too. Thickens the texture a bit. This was my second time making it. The first time making it, I cooked some chicken breast I had. I say save your chicken for a chicken main dish and just buy the canned stuff. Tastes the same and saves work. Now that I've used up Grandma's dry beans, I will try the jar beans and make it even easier.

Love how easy this recipe is! I used 2 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves instead of a can of chicken. I put them in the crock pot raw, then after 2 hours shredded them and added the meat back in for the remaining time. When there was about an hour left to go, I did a taste test and though the initial flavor was great, but then became pretty bland. So I added 1 Tbsp of oregano, 1/4 tsp cumin, 1/8 tsp chili powder, 1/8 tsp red pepper flakes. The end result was delicious! A huge hit for my guests. Everyone wanted the recipe!

Used a pound package of dried great northern white beans instead of canned. Cooked two frozen boneless chicken breast halves with the beans on the stove and cut them up after cooking. Added salsa, pepper jack cheese and salt to taste. Very good and simple to make in about half the time of using a slow cooker.

This is a great basic recipe. I’m a vegetarian, so we make it using TVP (textured vegetable protein) or meatless chicken. It’s so easy and gets a lot of flavor from the salsa. I add some Tabasco to turn up the heat a little. Delicious with corn chips as well! I’ve gotten many compliments.

I made this recipe on the stovetop and did a fiesta blend cheese instead of pepperjack cheese and the family gobbled it up. Even my 8 year old picky eater who was complaining the whole time I prepared it, ate her whole bowl. It was so easy and a hit with the family!

I love that this is so easy to throw together! I did use fresh skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, so I cooked on high instead for the 4-5 hrs to cook the chicken. Then we shredded the chicken and added it back into the crock pot. Great with a dollop of sour cream on top.

Used 1 can great northern beans, 1 can corn, 8oz pepper jack, can of chicken, and most of a jar of mango peach salsa. Let sit in the crock pot all afternoon on low and it was DELICIOUS! Great with tortilla chips or just some torn up tortillas. The mango peach salsa made it sweet but still had a little kick
Followed the recipe except for slow cooker. It was ready in 1/2 Hr.
For how easy it is, should be 6 stars. Use fresh boiled and shredded chicken instead. Canned chicken is always pretty gross, no matter the recipe. Hubby loves it!

I'd give this 4 1/2 stars if I could - 5 stars are reserved for really awesome gourmet type stuff.
We are camping in a motorhome and I was looking for a recipe using canned chicken that wasn't chicken salad. I had "most" of the ingredients onhand so here's what I used:
1 each 15 1/2 oz cans great northern beans and black beans, about 10 oz. of salsa (what was left in the jar in the fridge), 10 oz. can of chicken, about 1 1/2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese - and I threw in a 4 oz. can of mild, diced green chili's. I put it all in a saucepan and heated it over medium heat till the cheese melted. It was delish! I'm amazed that this simple recipe was sooooo good. I'm usually a "from scratch" cook but this was so good I'm going to be making it often. Thanks, Nblanzy for a winner!

Used a combination of white kidney beans and chickpeas and spiced cheddar cheese, instead, since actual ingredients not available. Added green onions at the end and a bit of salt and pepper. Wonderful easy meal to serve with a salad.
Love it! So easy! So tasty! Will make over and over again! I had a bigger bag of shredded chicken, that was my only change.

I always try a recipe as written first. As written, this is wonderful! Thank you so much. It just doesn't get any easier to make. It also makes a great base for trying variations. I'll most definitely make it again!
Great taste and easy to make. Will definitely make this again.
This is so easy! I've made this several times, my kids even like it!
Easy easy but tasted like i slaved all evening! Won chili cookoff and now i get requests to make all the time....
Big hit - Very well liked and so so easy!
This was super good. My two year old even licked her bowl she is such a picky eater. Next time I will make a bunch to freeze. Super easy for this Mother of 4 .
